subject: Post-demo: Rerank validation synthesis & proposed A/B plan
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@shoplane.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@marketly.io>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & next steps after demo

Thanks for the demo this morning, Priya — good overview. A couple quick clarifying items from our side before we loop in ML ops: 

- Can you share the short list of candidate rerank models we discussed (light latency vs. high-quality)?
- Would appreciate the benchmark artifacts (NDCG/MRR snapshots) against our sample workload we shared.
- We need a practical A/B plan that keeps our search latency under 120ms p50.

Happy to set a follow-up next week. Tom and I will review internally today.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, ShopLane

Attachment: shoplane-discovery-notes.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@shoplane.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & next steps after demo

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below. I also attached the raw eval artifacts and the prompt set we ran.

TL;DR / ask: We'll run a short canary A/B for 4 weeks with 10% traffic on the "balanced-rerank-v2" model (quantized) and fall back to your current ranker if p95 latency exceeds 200ms or NDCG drops >1.5 points. Can you confirm that trigger thresholds look acceptable?

1) Candidate models (short list):
  - balanced-rerank-v2 (8-bit quant, recommended start) — best mix of infer cost and NDCG uplift in our benchmarks
  - quality-rerank-xl (16-bit, slower) — +1.8 NDCG on holdout but ~2x token cost
  - fast-rerank-lite (distilled) — 40% lower latency, modest NDCG gains

2) Benchmarks we ran against your sample dataset: attached ndcg_mrr_summary_q3.csv; key takeaways below: 
  - NDCG@10: baseline (your current) = 0.342, balanced-rerank-v2 = 0.371 (+0.029)
  - MRR: baseline = 0.214, balanced-rerank-v2 = 0.236 (+0.022)
  - p50 latency (in our hosted env): balanced-rerank-v2 = 85ms, p95 = 178ms (sequence len median = 64 tokens)

3) Prompt set / regression concerns: we ran prompt-set-v2.txt (focused on session-context + category boosts). A few failure modes we flagged: handling of long-facet queries (sequence length > 150) shows quality drop for quantized weights; we recommend an explicit length-based routing rule for those queries to the quality-rerank-xl model during canary.

4) Proposed A/B plan (high-level):
  - 4-week canary, 10% randomized traffic, multi-metric gate (NDCG delta & latency SLO)
  - Monitoring: token-level cost, per-route p50/p95, NDCG on weekly holdout replays
  - Roll strategy: ramp to 50% if stable after 2 weeks; full rollout after 4 weeks subject to business sign-off

Next steps I suggest:
  - You confirm thresholds (latency/NDCG) and approve routing rule for long queries
  - We'll schedule 45min ops sync with your ML infra (Karthik and Laura will join) to wire up traces and the reroute fallback policy

Attaching: ndcg_mrr_summary_q3.csv, prompt-set-v2.txt, shoplane-discovery-notes.pdf

Thanks — available today 2–4pm PT for a quick call if that helps.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@marketly.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@shoplane.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & next steps after demo

Looping in a brief note from my side — sounds good overall. A couple questions for the ops sync:

- For the length-based routing, can Redwood expose the sequence length bucket as a trace attribute so we can slice latency vs quality in our dashboards?
- Are we able to set the canary to run only on search results with more than 2 user interactions (to avoid skew from cold queries)?

I'll bring these up in the sync. We prefer the balanced-rerank-v2 as the start.

Thanks,
Tom Baxter
Senior Eng, Search @ Marketly (consulting for ShopLane)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@shoplane.com>, Tom Baxter <tbaxter@marketly.io>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & next steps after demo

Hi Elena / Tom — Karthik here (runtime & infra). A few specifics on observability and the canary wiring so you're comfortable: 

- We'll expose sequence_length, route_variant, and model_version as trace attributes in the outgoing telemetry. You can query these via the Redwood Console trace API.
- Canary config we propose to use via the Console: 10% traffic, 4w duration, weekly holdout replays of 50k queries for offline NDCG/MRR. If any weekly delta (NDCG) < -0.8 points or p95 latency > 200ms we auto-fall back.
- For targeting interactive users only: we can add a traffic rule (interaction_count >= 2) — this is supported. Note this reduces sample size; to keep statistical power we'll also mirror 100% of traffic to an offline replay pipeline for additional analysis.

I'll add the canary config to the shared Drive folder and drop a short checklist for your infra team. Proposed ops sync: Thu 2026-10-07 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET. Does that work?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: canary-checklist.md (text)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@shoplane.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@marketly.io>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & next steps after demo

Thanks all — that level of detail is great and the thresholds look reasonable. Confirming:

- Approve balanced-rerank-v2 canary start (10% traffic, 4 weeks)
- Approve length-based routing to quality-rerank-xl for seq > 150
- Approve interaction_count >= 2 filter for canary (Tom: we'll accept smaller sample, mirror traffic for offline analysis)

We accept the auto-fallback triggers (NDCG drop -0.8 or p95 > 200ms). Please share the Drive folder and the canary checklist so our infra can prep.

Let's keep the Thu ops sync; I'll invite our ML infra lead.

Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, ShopLane
